overall_summary: Bitcoin is under clear pressure as ETF outflows persist, USDC supply shrinks, and hot jobs data push rate-hike odds, the dollar, and yields higher. Regulatory heat on MEXC plus fresh geopolitical strikes add to the risk-off tone while price sits on critical seventy-five thousand support. Extreme fear and heavy liquidations hint at capitulation, but near-term catalysts still point lower until support holds or macro cools.
key_points: Hot NFP lifts hike odds, dollar, and yields
Extreme fear and $1B liquidations signal washout
Geopolitics and FinCEN MEXC cut add risk-off

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Bleed Another $412M, IBIT Leads Exodus
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $411.9 million in net outflows on Friday November 6, with BlackRock's IBIT alone accounting for $403 million. That extends the recent drain to roughly $1.28 billion over five sessions and about $1.65 billion combined with Ether ETFs. Institutional demand is clearly absent right now, so traders should watch whether this keeps pressure on the $75,000 support zone even if spot price stabilizes over the weekend.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and weaker bid for any rebound

items.title: Crypto Liquidations Top $1B as Bitcoin Tests 11-Week Low
items.summary: More than $1 billion in leveraged positions were wiped out, overwhelmingly longs, as Bitcoin briefly traded down to about $74,780, its weakest level since late August. The cascade came with a sharp Nasdaq and AI-stock selloff plus stronger U.S. jobs data that raised rate-hike odds. Leverage has been flushed and Fear sits at extreme levels, so the immediate question for traders is whether $75,000 holds or gives way next week.
items.impact: Volatility elevated; support test decides next directional move

items.title: FinCEN Cuts MEXC Off From U.S. Financial System
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury's FinCEN issued an order severing crypto exchange MEXC Global from the American banking system over at least $16 billion in alleged illicit flows tied to Iran, North Korea, Russia and cybercrime. U.S. institutions will be barred from processing transfers once the order takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication. This is a major compliance hammer on a top-20 exchange and raises the regulatory risk premium across the sector.
items.impact: Heightened exchange and counterparty risk premium

items.title: Bitcoin Holds $76K but $75K Support Remains Critical
items.summary: After the tech-driven plunge and heavy ETF redemptions, Bitcoin has edged back above $76,000 into the weekend. Daily momentum is still soft and the next weekly support sits near $75,000. Traders need to treat this as an unresolved level: a confirmed hold or bounce would improve the setup, while a clean break opens lower targets.

items.title: Fear & Greed Index Hits Extreme Fear Near 25
items.summary: The crypto Fear and Greed Index has dropped into Extreme Fear territory around 25, the lowest reading in roughly three months. This matches the leverage flush and ETF outflows. Extreme readings often mark washed-out conditions where forced sellers are done, but they do not guarantee an immediate reversal, so position sizing and confirmation still matter more than the label.
items.impact: Contrarian bounce potential if support holds

items.title: USDC Circulating Supply Falls About $800 Million
items.summary: Circle's latest transparency window shows USDC redemptions outpaced new issuance by roughly $800 million over seven days, leaving circulating supply near $69.2 billion. Reserves remain fully backing the tokens, but shrinking stablecoin float removes dry powder that could otherwise chase risk assets. Traders should note it as another mild liquidity headwind alongside the ETF outflows.
items.impact: Reduced stablecoin liquidity available for crypto bids

items.title: October NFP Surges 165K, Far Above Forecasts
items.summary: The US added 165,000 jobs in October, crushing expectations near 60,000, while unemployment slipped to 4.1 percent. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4 percent and prior months were revised higher by a combined 84,000. This resilient labor market keeps the Fed focused on inflation rather than growth risks. Crypto traders should care because strong jobs data typically supports higher-for-longer rates and a firmer dollar, which often pressures risk assets including Bitcoin.
items.impact: Raises odds of tighter policy and stronger USD headwinds for BTC

items.title: December Fed Hike Odds Jump After Hot Jobs Data
items.summary: Futures markets pushed the probability of a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 meeting to roughly 75-80 percent after the strong payrolls print. Traders also pulled forward expectations for a subsequent move into early 2027. With inflation still elevated and the labor market firm, the path of least resistance is more restrictive policy. That environment usually means higher real yields and less liquidity support for crypto.
items.impact: Increases near-term rate-hike risk and discount-rate pressure

items.title: US Dollar Index Climbs Above 102 on Jobs Strength
items.summary: The dollar index jumped about 0.7 percent on Friday to close near 102.30, reclaiming key levels after the NFP surprise. Safe-haven flows earlier in the week had been mixed, but the labor data gave the greenback clear support. A stronger DXY tends to tighten global financial conditions. For Bitcoin and other risk assets this usually translates into selling pressure until the dollar impulse fades.
items.impact: Stronger USD historically correlates with crypto weakness

items.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Rises Toward 4.87 Percent
items.summary: The US 10-year yield climbed after the jobs report, finishing near 4.86 to 4.87 percent as markets priced firmer growth and higher rate odds. Bond prices fell while the curve showed some flattening at the front end. Higher yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets. Crypto traders watch this closely because sustained yield increases have repeatedly weighed on Bitcoin valuations.
items.impact: Higher yields tighten financial conditions for risk assets

items.title: Michigan Sentiment Beats as Inflation Expectations Ease
items.summary: University of Michigan preliminary consumer sentiment rose to 51.0 in early November from 48.0, beating the 48 consensus. One-year inflation expectations cooled to 4.3 percent from 4.7 percent and longer-run expectations edged down to 3.4 percent. The survey closed before the midterm results and the latest equity volatility. Softer inflation views offer a modest offset to the hawkish jobs signal, but cost-of-living concerns remain elevated.
items.impact: Mildly eases inflation fears but secondary to NFP signal

items.title: October CPI Due Tuesday November 10 at 8:30 ET
items.summary: No major US data prints today on Saturday, but the next high-impact release is the Consumer Price Index for October on Tuesday, November 10 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. Markets will watch both headline and core readings after September’s 3.7 percent year-over-year print. With December hike odds already elevated after NFP, a hot CPI could lock in further tightening expectations. This is the key event risk for rates, the dollar, and crypto into next week.
items.impact: Unresolved catalyst that will drive next leg in rates and USD

items.title: US Hits Iranian Air Defenses in Fresh Hormuz Strikes
items.summary: President Trump said the US carried out another round of limited strikes Friday on an Iranian air defense system on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling them minor and saying it was knocked out quickly. Iranian media reported explosions in the area. This comes right after the midterms and while Qatar mediates and Iran floats nuclear proposals. Crypto traders should watch because any Hormuz flare-up juicing oil prices hits risk appetite hard and keeps volatility elevated across markets.
items.impact: Raises oil risk premium and broad risk-off pressure on Bitcoin

items.title: Russian Ballistic Missiles Strike Kyiv Before Talks
items.summary: Russia fired ballistic missiles at Kyiv overnight into Saturday, injuring at least five people including a child, damaging residential buildings, the Northern Bridge, and energy facilities. Zelensky warned beforehand of infrastructure attacks. The barrage comes days ahead of US-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. Traders care because fresh escalation in Ukraine keeps European energy tight and overall geopolitical risk elevated, weighing on risk assets.
items.impact: Sustains energy and risk-off headwinds for crypto

items.title: Paraguay President Impeached Over Massive Bank Collapse
items.summary: Paraguay's Senate unanimously impeached President Santiago Peña Friday and placed him under house arrest over the collapse of Ueno Bank, which froze accounts for millions of people and sparked protests. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim leader. Peña had prior business ties to the bank and denies wrongdoing. This hits a previously stable South American growth story that had drawn foreign investment, so emerging-market risk sentiment takes a hit.
items.impact: Damages EM confidence and capital flows

items.title: Trump Names Hardliner Stephen Miller Chief of Staff
items.summary: After the Republican midterm thrashing, President Trump replaced Chief of Staff Susie Wiles with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, effective Monday. Miller is the architect of hardline immigration policies and known for aggressive tactics. Wiles moves to the political side. This signals Trump intends to dig in against a Democratic Congress rather than moderate, raising the odds of sharper domestic and foreign policy fights that could spill into markets.
items.impact: Adds US political uncertainty and potential policy volatility

items.title: US Sanctions Canadian Firms for Helping Iran Evade Rules
items.summary: The US Treasury sanctioned eight Canadian money-exchange businesses Friday for facilitating transactions with sanctioned Iranian entities, including converting rials into digital assets and links to the IRGC. Some were also tied to a major drug trafficker. It is part of the ongoing Operation Economic Outcast pressure campaign. This keeps financial squeeze on Iran alive even as military and diplomatic tracks run in parallel, with a direct crypto angle via digital asset channels.
items.impact: Tightens Iran funding channels; minor direct crypto compliance risk

items.title: US Offers $20 Million Reward for Iran Nuclear Intel
items.summary: US Central Command announced a Rewards for Justice offer of up to 20 million dollars plus possible relocation for information on Iran's nuclear program facilities, equipment, and personnel. It dropped late Friday alongside the latest strikes. Combined with Trump weighing bigger decisions post-midterms and Qatar still mediating, it underscores unresolved nuclear issues remain the core sticking point. Markets stay sensitive to any signal that talks collapse or escalate further.
items.impact: Keeps nuclear and escalation overhang on oil and risk assets
